title: ByteDance's Zhang Yiming Overtakes Mukesh Ambani as Asia's Second-Richest Person
excerpt: The TikTok founder's net worth surged to $92.8 billion on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, powered by ByteDance's AI push and the resolution of TikTok's US regulatory overhang.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Zhang Yiming's net worth reached $92.8 billion, making him Asia's second-richest person.
  • His fortune surged over $24 billion after ByteDance's valuation was reassessed.
  • ByteDance plans to invest $70 billion in AI by 2026, funded by 2025 profits.
  • Gautam Adani remains the richest in Asia at $117.4 billion, while Ambani is third at $86.9 billion.

  • ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming's net worth reached $92.8 billion, vaulting him past Mukesh Ambani to become Asia's second-richest person on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index
  • Zhang's fortune jumped more than $24 billion after Bloomberg lowered its risk discount on ByteDance's valuation from 25% to 10%, reflecting the completed sale of TikTok's US operations
  • ByteDance is planning up to $70 billion in AI spending in 2026, funded largely by $50 billion in 2025 profits, as its Doubao chatbot crossed 300 million monthly users
  • Gautam Adani remains Asia's richest person at $117.4 billion, while Ambani slipped to third at $86.9 billion

ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming has surpassed Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani to become Asia's second-richest person, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Zhang's net worth climbed to $92.8 billion after a sharp upward revision of ByteDance's valuation, driven by the company's expanding AI business and the resolution of years of regulatory uncertainty around TikTok in the United States.

The shift marks a dramatic reshuffling of Asia's wealth hierarchy. Gautam Adani holds the top position at $117.4 billion, while Ambani has dropped to third at $86.9 billion, according to Bloomberg.

A $24 Billion Wealth Surge

Zhang's fortune jumped by more than $24 billion after Bloomberg reassessed ByteDance's valuation using filings from institutional investors including BlackRock, Fidelity Investments, T. Rowe Price, HSG and General Atlantic, according to a Bloomberg report published on June 3.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=i8bBx7EZ1Rk

The index had previously applied a 25% risk discount to ByteDance's valuation after the US House of Representatives passed a bill in March 2024 seeking to ban TikTok unless its Chinese owner divested the app. That discount was lowered to 10% on June 2 to reflect the completion of TikTok's US sale and post-spinoff valuations reported by institutional investors in late May regulatory filings.

"ByteDance is reportedly planning to spend up to $70 billion in 2026 to expand its AI capabilities and challenge leading US tech companies in the space."

"The jump in valuation reflects the company's strong fundamentals and the success of its apps such as Doubao in China. The developments in the US are unlikely to have a major negative impact."

— Amy Lin, Analyst, Capital Securities

Earlier in 2026, a consortium led by Oracle, Silver Lake and Abu Dhabi-based MGX took over TikTok's US operations, ending years of political and regulatory uncertainty. Zhang first became China's richest person in 2025, was briefly overtaken, and reclaimed the title earlier this year.

AI and Doubao Power ByteDance's Rise

Two forces have propelled ByteDance's valuation. TikTok continues to perform as a dominant global short-video platform. But it is ByteDance's AI ambitions that have increasingly caught investor attention.

The company's Doubao AI chatbot has amassed more than 300 million monthly users, making it China's most popular AI application, according to Bloomberg. ByteDance is reportedly planning to spend up to $70 billion in 2026 to expand its AI capabilities and challenge leading US tech companies in the space. Much of that spending is expected to come from approximately $50 billion in profit ByteDance earned in 2025.

"Removing the US overhang unlocked the re-rating of the remaining ByteDance entity. Even with the re-rating, the valuation still looks cheap on fundamentals."

— Ke Yan, Tech Analyst, DZT Research

Zhang's fortune has grown more than sevenfold since March 2019, when Bloomberg first began tracking his wealth at approximately $13 billion. ByteDance, which remains privately held, is also considered a strong candidate for an eventual initial public offering.

What It Means for Ambani and Indian Billionaires

For Mukesh Ambani, the ranking shift comes even as Reliance Industries continues to expand across telecom, retail and energy. His net worth of $86.9 billion on Bloomberg's list reflects a gap of nearly $6 billion behind Zhang — a margin that widened sharply after ByteDance's valuation rerating.

The divergence between Bloomberg and Forbes rankings is worth noting: Forbes' real-time billionaire tracker still lists Ambani as Asia's richest person at $89.5 billion, with Adani second at $86.3 billion and Zhang third at $69.3 billion. The discrepancy stems from different valuation methodologies for privately held companies like ByteDance.

What's Next

ByteDance's AI Ambitions
›Doubao AI chatbot has over 300 million monthly users.
›ByteDance plans $70 billion AI investment by 2026.
›Investment largely funded by $50 billion in 2025 profits.

ByteDance's planned $70 billion AI investment in 2026 will be closely watched. If the company succeeds in establishing itself as a global AI leader alongside its social media dominance, Zhang's wealth could continue to climb. The company's potential IPO, long speculated but never confirmed, would provide the most transparent valuation yet of what has become one of the world's most powerful private tech companies.

For now, the ranking change underscores how AI-driven growth and regulatory clarity can rapidly redraw the global wealth map — pushing a Chinese tech entrepreneur past one of India's most established industrialists in a matter of weeks.
